corrections.caveats: Weak evidence, tier C at most. The only number is one anecdote from the QtAV 1.3.3 announcement thread on the Qt forum ('A video player based on Qt and FFmpeg', forum.qt.io/post/21312, 2014 era), posted by the project author: about 10% less CPU than VLC for a 10-bit H.264 video on an HTC Butterfly S. forum.qt.io does not resolve from this environment, so the page was NOT opened and the figure comes from WebSearch snippets only (snippet only, seen independently by the searcher and the verifier). No VLC version, decoder path (VLC's software vs QtAV's), build, video file, or CPU model is given, and it is a single-device test with no methodology. A search snippet also showed a user reporting that VLC plays full-HD video more smoothly than QtAV, so the claim is contested. The repo README makes no performance claim (only that it was the first player to render 10-bit in OpenGL ES2, which VLC, XBMC and mplayer did not support at the time). The wiki pages carry unquantified claims only: 'The Most Efficient VDA Decoder on OSX' (April 2015) says 'The performance is the best now. Better than any other players.', and 'Hardware Accelerated Decoding' says DirectCopy mode is 'faster than potplayer, lavfilters+mpc, and may be the fastest one'; neither has numbers. The README says the author is no longer developing QtAV and points users to his mdk-sdk; the 2025 commits are a contributor's Vulkan renderer.

notes: Real, notable project (4.3k stars, 1.5k forks, listed on the FFmpeg projects page) but the speed evidence is one unopened author forum anecdote (~10% less CPU than VLC on one Android phone, 2014) plus unquantified wiki claims; kept at C on snippet-only evidence, with D the fallback if the orchestrator requires an opened numbers page. Shortcomings to record: snippet-only single-device anecdote, no methodology or VLC version, contested by a user report, author stopped development (stale, last commit 2025-08-15 by a contributor). Metadata checked on github.com: LGPL-2.1 library plus GPL-3.0 player example, not a fork, not shown as archived.
